content: 1. Sodium picosulfate is converted into its active drug form in the body. 2. Ceftibuten increases the toxicity of streptomycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Close monitoring is required. 3. Cephalosporins, including ceftibuten, may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Ceftibuten can increase the levels or effects of sulfasalazine due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Ceftibuten may increase the levels or effects of sulindac through similar competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is also unknown. 6. Ceftibuten and temocillin may increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Close monitoring is advised. 7. Ceftibuten may decrease the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 8. Ceftibuten may reduce the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 9. Ceftibuten increases the toxicity of tobramycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins, in general, may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 10. Ceftibuten may increase the levels or effects of tolfenamic acid due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Ceftibuten may increase the levels or effects of tolmetin through similar competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Ceftibuten may reduce the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 13. Ceftibuten decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administration of the live bacterial vaccine should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 14. Ceftibuten may increase the levels or effects of valganciclovir due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Ceftibuten and voclosporin may increase each other's toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 16. Ceftibuten may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ceftibuten may increase the levels or effects of willow bark due to competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Zinc may decrease the levels or effects of ceftibuten by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider administering oral zinc salts at least three hours after ceftibuten. 19. Common adverse effects of ceftibuten include increased blood urea nitrogen (4%), nausea (4%), diarrhea (3%), headache (3%), increased eosinophils (3%), decreased hemoglobin (2%), dyspepsia (2%), thrombocytosis (2%), abdominal pain (1%), dizziness (1%), increased ALT (1%), increased bilirubin (1%), vomiting (1%), and anorexia. 20. Less common adverse effects include candidiasis, constipation, dysuria, agitation, fatigue, insomnia, irritability, paresthesia, rigors, diaper rash, urticaria, dry mouth, dyspnea, nasal congestion, increased transaminases, increased creatinine, leukopenia, and documented hypersensitivity. 21. For diabetic patients, note that the oral suspension contains 1 gram of sucrose per teaspoon. 22. Dosage adjustments are necessary in cases of severe renal impairment. Prolonged use may result in superinfection. Use caution in patients with seizure disorders, as ceftibuten may cause antibiotic-associated colitis. 23. Pregnancy Category B: Studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 24. Lactation: Excretion in breast milk is unknown; use with caution. 25. Ceftibuten is a third-generation cephalosporin with bactericidal activity. It inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to one or more penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), thereby disrupting cell wall mucopeptide synthesis. 26. Approximately 56% of the drug is excreted in urine, and 39% is excreted in feces. Its volume of distribution is 21 L/kg. 27.
